eyebrow: Lesson 22 · B1 · Good Table Manners · 20 câu
heading: Waiting and Cutlery
source: Bài đọc phỏng theo Good Table Manners – Ann Ingalls (The Child's World, 2013), tr. 8–11.
credit: Tranh minh hoạ: Ronnie Rooney, trong Good Table Manners (The Child's World, 2013). Dùng cho mục đích học tập.

paras.label: A
paras.text: Before you start eating, wait until everyone has been {served|served}. In many homes, the polite signal to begin is when the hosts pick up their forks.

paras.label: B
paras.text: Don't {reach across|reach across} the table for food. Instead, ask someone to pass it to you, and when dishes go round, pass them to your left. Take only as much as you think you can eat. Don't {pile|pile} a mountain of mashed potato on your plate!

paras.label: C
paras.text: Customs are not the same everywhere. In Afghanistan, it is polite for guests to eat first, and they are expected to eat the most! So if you ever visit, don't be shy about your {appetite|appetite}.

paras.label: D
paras.text: At a {formal|formal} dinner, you may see several knives and forks, and some may even be placed above your plate. Don't panic! Start with the {cutlery|cutlery} on the outside (Americans call it silverware) and work your way in. And never use your knife as a {toothpick|toothpick}!

paras.label: E
paras.text: Your bread plate sits to the left of your dinner plate. Choose a piece of bread or a roll, {tear off|tear off} a small piece and butter just that piece. Don't try to rip the whole roll apart with your teeth, or {crumbs|crumbs} might fly across the table!

parts.title: Part 1 · Which paragraph?
parts.instr: Đoạn nào (A–E) chứa thông tin dưới đây?

items.label: A paragraph that explains which knives and forks to use first
items.why: Đoạn D: *Start with the cutlery on the outside.*

items.label: A paragraph that describes the signal to start eating
items.why: Đoạn A: chủ nhà cầm dĩa lên.

items.label: A paragraph that warns you not to take too much food
items.why: Đoạn B: *Don't pile a mountain of mashed potato.*

items.label: A paragraph that explains how to eat bread politely
items.why: Đoạn E: xé miếng nhỏ, phết bơ.

items.label: A paragraph about a country where guests are expected to eat a lot

parts.title: Part 2 · Reading comprehension
parts.instr: Chọn đáp án đúng hoặc True / False.

questions.q: When is it polite to start eating?
options: when everyone has been served and the hosts begin
as soon as your food arrives
questions.why: *wait until everyone has been served… the hosts pick up their forks.*

questions.q: The writer says you should pass dishes to your right.
What should you do if a dish is too far away from you?
options: Stand up and reach for it.
Wait until the end of the meal.
questions.why: *ask someone to pass it to you.*

questions.q: In Afghanistan, guests are expected to eat less than their hosts.
questions.why: Sai. *they are expected to eat the most!*

questions.q: If there are several forks, which one should you use first?
options: the one closest to the plate
questions.why: *Start with the cutlery on the outside.*

questions.q: Why does the writer warn about crumbs in (E)?
options: Biting into a whole roll can make a mess.
Crumbs are bad for your teeth.
Bread should never be eaten at dinner.
questions.why: *Don't try to rip the whole roll apart with your teeth, or crumbs might fly.*

parts.title: Part 3 · Picture tasks
parts.instr: Quan sát tranh minh hoạ trong sách và trả lời.

questions.q: What is the boy doing wrong?
questions.why: Đoạn B: *Don't reach across the table.*
questions.alt: A boy leans over the table and stretches his arm across a girl's plate to grab food from a basket

questions.q: What should the boy have done instead?
options: asked someone to pass the food
questions.why: *ask someone to pass it to you.*
questions.alt: A boy leans over the table and stretches his arm across a girl's plate to grab food from a basket

questions.q: Which paragraph would help this boy most?
questions.why: Đoạn D: dùng dao dĩa từ ngoài vào trong.
questions.alt: A boy at a table holds up a fork in each hand and looks confused by all the knives and forks around his plate

parts.title: Part 4 · Gapped text
parts.instr: Đọc đoạn văn ngắn và chọn câu phù hợp cho mỗi chỗ trống. Có 2 câu thừa.
parts.text: Last month, my aunt took me to a smart restaurant to celebrate her birthday. [1] I had no idea which one to use. [2] Then the waiter brought a basket of warm bread rolls. [3]
options: The restaurant was closed, so we went home.
When I sat down, I saw three forks and two knives next to my plate.
There was only a spoon on the table, so I ate everything with it.
Luckily, my aunt whispered, "Start from the outside and work your way in."
I tore off a small piece and buttered it, just like everyone else.

items.why: Cần chỗ cho *which one* → nhiều dao dĩa.
Ăn bánh mì đúng cách (đoạn E).

parts.title: Part 5 · Words in context
parts.instr: Đoán nghĩa của từ/cụm từ dựa vào ngữ cảnh.

questions.q: *Don't reach across the table* (B). To **reach across** means to…
options: stretch your arm over something to get it

questions.q: *Don't pile a mountain of mashed potato on your plate!* (B). Here, **a mountain of** means…
*…never use your knife as a toothpick!* (D). A **toothpick** is…
options: a small stick for cleaning between your teeth
